## Contents
### Page 1
Explicit cocycles for graph Hall algebrasLluis Eriksson
4 November 2026Research draft, candidate 2: external assessment pendingAbstractFor the reduced simplicial set whose simplices are subgraphs of a finite labelled undi-
rected multigraph equipped with ordered partitions of their vertices, we construct explicit
mod-two cohomology classes indexed by subgraphs. Vertex restriction pulls a supported
top-dimensional cochain into a global cocycle. Permutation cycles pair with these classes
as a Kronecker basis, while a vertex filtration bounds the total cohomology dimension
using augmented Boolean order complexes. Alexander–Whitney multiplication recov-
ers the graph Hall product. This proves the finite-graph Hall/cohomology identification
stated as Conjecture 1.1 by Toury. The construction concerns labelled subgraphs, not
isomorphism classes of rooted forests. Exact finite checks accompany the proof; priority
and external mathematical assessment remain pending.1 The graph model and the statementLet G = (V, E) be a finite labelled undirected graph. The finite edge set has an endpoint
map to unordered vertex pairs, allowing repeated endpoints (loops) and distinct labelled
edges with equal endpoint pairs. A subgraph H specifies S ⊆ V and any subset of ambient
edge identities with both endpoints in S. It need not be induced in G. Write H|A for the
induced restriction of H to A ⊆ V , and include the empty graph.
We use the simplicial graph model of Bergner et al. [2], also described in [3, 4]. The
ordered-partition description and its symmetry also appear in [1, Examples 3.9 and 5.11];
those constructions are background, rather than claims of novelty here. In degree k, a simplex
is a subgraph H together with an ordered partition (B1, . . . , Bk) of V(H), permitting empty
blocks. Degree zero has one element. Endpoint faces delete the first or last block, restrictingH to the remaining vertices. Face di, 0 < i < k, merges Bi and Bi+1. Degeneracies insert
an empty block. Thus a normalized simplex has all its blocks nonempty, and its degree is at
most |V |.
The graph Hall algebra H(G; F2) has a basis [H] indexed by all actual subgraphs. Its
unit is [∅]. If A, B intersect in a vertex, set [A][B] = 0. Otherwise set
[A][B] = ∑D⊆EG(V(A),V(B))[A ⨿ B + D]. (1)
Here the summand retains exactly the internal edges of A and B and adds D as cross edges.
This is the labelled graph Hall product [4, Proposition 4.4.1]; give [H] degree | V(H)|.Theorem 1. There is a canonical graded algebra isomorphismΦG : H(G; F2) −→ H∗(|XG|; F2).For a nonempty H on S, its image is represented by the pullback, under vertex restriction
to S, of the cochain supported on one singleton-block ordering of H. Its cohomology class is
independent of that ordering.1



### Page 2
This statement addresses the finite-graph statement of [4, Conjecture 1.1]. It identifies
a cohomology algebra, not a homotopy type or the even-degree polyhedral-product space
constructed in that paper. No assertion is made about arbitrary reduced 2-Segal sets. In
particular, the construction does not pass to isomorphism classes of unlabelled graphs or to
a rooted-tree cut algebra.2 A finite dimension boundAll chains and cochains below are normalized and have coefficients in F2. Let FpC∗(XG)
be generated by simplices whose underlying graph has at most p vertices. This is a finite
filtration by subcomplexes: interior faces preserve the graph and endpoint faces decrease its
vertex set.Lemma 2. The sum of the Betti numbers of XG is at most the number of subgraphs of G.
Proof. For p > 0, the quotient FpC∗/Fp−1C∗ is a direct sum over subgraphs H with exactlyp vertices. Each summand has the ordered partitions of V(H) into k nonempty blocks as its
degree-k basis. Its differential merges adjacent blocks; endpoint faces vanish in the quotient.
When p ≥ 2, associate (B1, . . . , Bk) to the chain of proper nonempty subsetsB1 ⊊ B1 ∪ B2 ⊊ · · · ⊊ B1 ∪ · · · ∪ Bk−1.This identifies the summand with the augmented simplicial chains of the proper Boolean
order complex, shifted up by two degrees. For k = 1 the chain of subsets is empty and
represents the augmentation in degree −1. Removing a proper initial union merges the
corresponding adjacent blocks, so the differentials agree over F2.
The proper Boolean order complex is the barycentric subdivision of the boundary of the
(p − 1)-simplex. Its reduced homology is one-dimensional in degree p − 2 and zero otherwise.
The shifted summand therefore has one homology generator, in degree p. For p = 1 this
conclusion follows directly from the single degree-one partition. For p = 0, the empty graph
contributes the basepoint in degree zero.
For a short exact sequence of finite chain complexes, the long exact sequence in homology
bounds the total homology dimension of the middle complex by the sum of those of the
other two. Apply this successively to the vertex filtration. Each subgraph contributes one
to the resulting upper bound. Normalized simplicial homology computes the homology of
the realization; over a field its Betti numbers equal those of cohomology.3 Cycles and dual cocyclesFor a nonempty subgraph H on S, put p = |S|. DefinezH = ∑σ∈Ord(S)(H; {σ1}, . . . , {σp}), (2)
where Ord(S) denotes all linear orderings of S.Lemma 3. The chain zH is a cycle.
Proof. Every internal face merges two adjacent singleton blocks. Exactly two orderings yield
that face, differing by swapping those vertices. Endpoint faces also pair: for every v ∈ S and
every ordering of S \ {v}, placing v at the beginning or at the end yields the same induced
graph H|S\{v} and the same residual ordering. All pairs cancel over F2. For p = 1, the two
endpoints both equal the basepoint and cancel.
2



### Page 3
For a fixed S ⊆ V , define vertex restriction on all simplices, including degenerate ones,
byρS (H; B1, . . . , Bk) = (H|S ; B1 ∩ S, . . . , Bk ∩ S).Its target is XG|S . Intersection commutes with adjacent union, endpoint deletion and inser-
tion of empty blocks. Hence ρS is a simplicial map. On normalized cochains a restricted
simplex with an empty block contributes zero.
Choose an ordering ω of S. In degree p of XG|S , let aH,ω be the cochain taking value
one precisely on (H; {ω1}, . . . , {ωp}) and zero on every other normalized p-simplex. As the
target has no nondegenerate simplices in degree p + 1, this is a cocycle. SetαH,ω = ρ∗S aH,ω. (3)
Explicitly, it is one on a simplex precisely when its restriction to S is that chosen ordered
singleton simplex of H.Proposition 4. For subgraphs H, K with the same number of vertices,⟨αH,ω, zK ⟩ ={1 H = K,0 H̸ = K.The classes [αH,ω], together with the degree-zero unit, form a basis of the cohomology of XG.
Proof. A nonzero evaluation requires S = V(H) to be contained in V(K). Equal cardinality
forces equality of these vertex sets. It then requires exactly the same edge set and the chosen
ordering. Precisely one term of (2) contributes when H = K. Thus the displayed pairing is a
Kronecker pairing. Since a coboundary vanishes on every cycle, the classes are independent.
Their total number is the upper bound in Lemma 2, so they are a basis. For G empty, both
sides have only the degree-zero unit.Lemma 5. The class [αH,ω] is independent of ω.
Proof. It suffices to exchange an adjacent pair in an ordering of S. For p ≥ 2, in XG|S take
the degree-(p − 1) cochain supported on H with that pair merged into a doubleton block and
every other block unchanged. Its coboundary is the sum of the two ordered top cochains.
Indeed, a normalized p-simplex there must have all p vertices in singleton blocks; only the
two splittings of the specified doubleton yield the supported face. Endpoint faces have fewer
vertices and do not contribute. Pulling back proves the claim. When p = 1 there is only one
ordering.4 MultiplicationWrite αH for a representative with an arbitrary chosen order, and use brackets when passing
to its order-independent class.Proof of Theorem 1. Define ΦG([H]) = [αH ] for nonempty H and send the empty graph
to the degree-zero unit. Proposition 4 makes this a graded vector space isomorphism. It
remains to check multiplication.
Let A, B have vertex sets S, T and degrees p, q > 0. The Alexander–Whitney product
evaluates αA on the front p-face and αB on the back q-face of a (p + q)-simplex. These two
faces retain respectively its first p and last q vertex blocks. If S ∩ T is nonempty, a shared
vertex would have to occur in both disjoint groups of blocks. Thus the cochain product is
identically zero.
3



### Page 4
Suppose S ∩ T = ∅. Restrict the simplex to S ∪ T . For a nonzero product its first prestricted blocks must be the ordered singletons of A, and its last q restricted blocks the
ordered singletons of B. The graph restricted to S must equal A, and that restricted toT must equal B. The only unconstrained edges of the restricted graph are ambient edges
between S and T . Consequently there is a cochain identityαA ⌣ αB = ∑D⊆EG(S,T )αA⨿B+D, ωS ωT ,where the order on the right is concatenation and each cochain is pulled back from XG|S∪T .
This identity also accounts for additional ambient vertices: they disappear under restriction
and cannot change the required singleton blocks. Lemma 5 allows replacement of concate-
nated orders by the chosen orders in cohomology. This gives exactly (1). The degree-zero
unit acts as the constant cochain one. Therefore ΦG is an algebra isomorphism. The absence
of a choice in its cohomology classes proves the asserted canonicity.5 Finite verification and scope of evidenceThe companion files graph_chains.py and verify.py run with Python 3.10 or later, with-
out third-party dependencies, using python verify.py. The exact code hashes and captured
output are in the accompanying SHA-256 manifest and verification-results.json. The
additional script verify_extension.py and extension-results.json check loops and re-
peated endpoint pairs. The three-vertex mixed fixture has one loop at vertex 0, two labelled
edges between 0 and 1, and two between 1 and 2. The supplied programs use normalized
chain matrices and exact elimination over F2. They check d2 = 0, cocycle closure, cycle
pairings and Alexander–Whitney multiplication modulo coboundaries. They supply controls
for the construction, not a replacement for its proof.

The product counts include positive degrees whose sum is at most the vertex count. Larger
degrees vanish by dimension. The unit is handled in the proof, not in those pair loops.
The code and proof were developed in the same assistant context; the computations do not
constitute independent review.
The proof applies to finite labelled undirected multigraphs with loops over F2. For a
fixed subgraph H, the filtration summand depends only on its vertex set. Restriction retains
precisely the labelled edge identities whose endpoints survive. Thus the cycle cancellations,
4



### Page 5
cocycles and order exchange do not require simplicity. In the product argument every re-
tained edge is internal to one of the two disjoint vertex sets or crosses between them. Loops
are internal and parallel edge identities remain separate choices. This partitions the allowed
edge sets exactly as in (1). We assert no integral or odd-characteristic version, identification
of homotopy types, or result about interacting quantum fields. The theorem must be distin-
guished from Toury’s already constructed even-degree polyhedral-product realization. The
exact graph model and literal labelled-subgraph Hall multiplication are essential.6 Model assessments and review contextThis draft was developed with AI assistance in a Codex chat, including literature triage,
proof construction and verification code. The same assistant performed the internal checks.
No separate model assessment of this exact PDF, human peer review, formal verification,
editorial acceptance or importance rating has yet been obtained. No stars are assigned here.
Requested model names or a product label do not authenticate the effective model identity
or reasoning effort. Targeted bibliographic searches have not established worldwide priority.
Lluis Eriksson is also AIRR’s founder, registry operator and responsible editor (https:
//airr.science/governance/); this is a disclosed author–operator conflict. No editorial
decision is recorded in this draft. Earlier small graph computations and the formulations of
the problem are credited to the sources below.References[1] I. Contreras, R. A. Mehta and W. H. Stern, Frobenius and commutative pseudomonoids
in the bicategory of spans, arXiv:2311.15342v2 (2024), Examples 3.9 and 5.11. https:
//arxiv.org/abs/2311.15342.
[2] J. E. Bergner, A. M. Osorno, V. Ozornova, M. Rovelli and C. I. Scheimbauer, 2-Segal sets
and the Waldhausen construction, Topology and its Applications 235 (2018), 445–484.
doi:10.1016/j.topol.2017.12.009.
[3] J. E. Bergner, Combinatorial examples and applications of 2-Segal sets,
arXiv:2411.18544v1 (2024). https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18544.
[4] L. Toury, Hall algebras of graphs and rooted trees, arXiv:2609.16849v1 (2026), Conjecture
1.1 and Sections 4.1, 4.7. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16849.
[5] J. Bergner (joint work with N. Kuhn and I. Zakharevich), 2-Segal sets, algebraic K-
theory, and Hall algebras, in Homotopy Theory, Oberwolfach Report 36/2019. https:
//doi.org/10.4171/OWR/2019/36.
